descriptionChirho: To engage in physical or verbal conflict, to fight or contend with another party. Used in Niphal (passive/reciprocal) and Hiphil across legal and narrative contexts: two Hebrew men fighting (Exod 2:13), men striving together and striking a pregnant woman (Exod 21:22; Deut 25:11), fighting in the camp (Lev 24:10), quarreling at the waters of Meribah (2 Sam 14:6), Korah's company contending against Moses (Num 26:9), and David striving against Aram (Ps 60:1 superscription). All stems and conjugations -- Niphal imperfect/consecutive/participle, Hiphil perfect/infinitive -- express the same core meaning of interpersonal or inter-group conflict. Multilingual glosses consistently render: Ar. takhasama/ta'araka, Ger. kaempfen/struggle, Sp. rineron/contendieron, Hin. lade/ladenge, Kor. ssawotda/datueotda.
